So both non-.text cuts are unambiguous and neither falls mid-run.

THE 22 FUNCTIONS, in .text order: init_enemy_vars 0x80050054, format_brain 0x80050394, SetEnemyObj 0x80050618, fn_800508A0, fn_80050910, AllocEnemy 0x8005094C, LoadEnemy 0x80050B8C, fn_80050DD8, GetEnemyType 0x80050FB0, fn_800510A4, fn_80051164, fn_800511D0, fn_80051480, fn_80051568, fn_800516F8, fn_80051C78, fn_80051E1C, EnemyTypePrefix 0x80051F64, EnemyTypeDesc 0x80051FA0, EnemyDescType 0x80051FDC, fn_8005207C, fn_800520C8. Three file-scope statics travel with them and their sole consumers are all inside the block: `static char sBossGenName[] = "BOSSGEN"` (read by EnemyDescType, .sdata2 0x80346AA4), `static s32 PlayersAverageLevel(void)` (called only by format_brain), `static char* findWorldName(s32 world)` (called only by fn_80051E1C, twice). gamemain.c is left with 28 shared .text functions: the GAMEDEFS prefix default_options / fn_80052134 / fn_800521E8 (see claim.SM_gamedefs-obj-is-at-most-two-gc-functions-not-three-because-the-sdata2-pool-interleaves-fn800521e8-with-gamemains.20260904.v1) and do_stats_display 0x800522E8 .. fn_80055AFC.

THE PIN CASCADE, counted rather than guessed. gamemain's remaining pins are fn_80054E78 (stays), fn_80051480 and fn_800511D0 -- and the latter TWO are inside the block, so they MIGRATE unit key exactly as DoWorldAnimation did in phase 1. game/enemy/enemy carries THIRTEEN rules: move_logic22, move_logic00, damage_enemy, do_enemies, fn_8004646C, closest_enemy, move_logic02, move_logic04, move_logic14, move_logic15, move_logic30, gendir_8004FBC8, find_neighbor_milestone. THREE are instruction_permutation rules -- move_logic22, move_logic00, fn_8004646C -- and adding 22 functions to the TU renumbers its anonymous pool, so each needs `python tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_rederive_pin.py game/enemy/enemy <fn> --apply` followed by `python configure.py`. Phase 1 measured that exact cycle four times on gauntworld's two permutation pins: every abort was a pure `@NNNN` renumber, every body hash returned unchanged, and every rule replayed.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Take `python tools/gdl/fuzzy.py game/enemy/enemy` and `... game/game/gamemain` row by row before the move and again after the first successful object build. Any row that drops is an inlining event; if more than a handful drop, the reversal/hoist question has to be answered for the whole block rather than one function, and the phase should be reverted rather than patched.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral for every function that neither gains nor loses an inline expansion; a gained inline lengthens OUR stream against the target and a lost one shortens it, which is the direction fn_80057024 moved (292 vs target 362) when its two InLevel expansions were lost in phase 1.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- no build was run with the enemy boundaries in place, and no callee/caller pair across the new boundary was checked for a gained or lost inline expansion.
hypothesis.statement: The enemy-block move is a strictly EASIER repetition of the gauntworld move, and the one new cost is the inlining screen over a much larger callee surface. Its boundaries need no discovery (all three cuts are exact and derived above), its GAMEDEFS complication is already resolved (gamemain simply keeps the prefix, which is the status quo for those bytes), and its declaration port is the same operation on the same source file. The unmeasured risk is claim.law.SM_moving-a-function-between-tus-...20260904.v1 in the enemy direction: enemy.c is 7612 lines and the 22 arrivals expose a far larger set of callees to a far larger set of callers than gauntworld's 24 did.
